title: Senior's toolkit: remotes and pull requests
summary: fetch --prune, tracking branches, safe force-pushes, range-diff, gh and tags: the daily team workflow.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: remotes and pull requests
steps.body: Working with a team is mostly fetch, branch, push and review. These are the forms that keep you in sync without overwriting anyone.

toolkit.what: Downloads new commits and deletes your remote-tracking refs for branches that were deleted on the server.
flags: drop `origin/x` when `x` is gone on the remote
toolkit.when: every morning, and before you rebase

toolkit.what: Lists local branches with their upstream and how far ahead or behind they are. `[origin/x: gone]` marks branches whose PR was merged and deleted.
flags: branches already contained in main, safe to delete

toolkit.what: Creates a branch from an exact starting point, usually a fresh `origin/main`, not whatever local main happens to be.
flags: set the upstream when starting from a remote branch

toolkit.what: Pushes the current branch under the same name and remembers it as the upstream, so later `git push` and `git pull` need no arguments.
flags: the current branch, whatever its name

toolkit.what: Replays your local commits on top of what others pushed, instead of adding a merge commit for every pull.
flags: config to make rebase the default
toolkit.when: your push was rejected because the remote moved

toolkit.what: Force-pushes your rewritten branch, but refuses if someone else pushed to it since your last fetch.
flags: only overwrite what you have already seen
also check that you integrated what you fetched
toolkit.when: after a rebase of your own PR branch

toolkit.what: Compares two versions of a branch commit by commit. Shows a reviewer what really changed after a rebase and force-push.
flags: your local branch against what is on the server
three-argument form with an explicit base
toolkit.when: before you force-push, or when re-reviewing a PR

toolkit.what: Fetches a pull request into a local branch so you can run it, not just read it. Works for PRs from forks too.
flags: open a draft PR using your commit messages
the status of its CI checks

steps.prompt: Match each command to the question it answers.
pairs: which local branches are ahead, behind or gone?
what did my rebase change, commit by commit?
which branches were deleted on the server?
is CI green on my pull request?
which branches are safe to delete?

steps.prompt: `git push` fails with `! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first)`. A teammate pushed while you were working. You have two local commits. What do you run?
options: `git pull --rebase`, run the tests, then `git push`
Delete your clone and clone again
steps.explain: The remote has commits you do not. `pull --rebase` fetches them and replays your two commits on top, so the push becomes a fast-forward. `--force` would delete your teammate's work; `reset --hard` would delete yours.

steps.prompt: Refresh your view of the remote, then publish a rebased PR branch without risking a teammate's push.
steps.explain: `--prune` removes refs for deleted branches. `--force-with-lease` overwrites only the version you last fetched; plain `--force` overwrites anything.

steps.prompt: You force-pushed your rebased PR. The reviewer writes: "I can't tell what changed since my last review." What do you give them?
options: The output of `git range-diff` between the old tip and the new tip
steps.explain: `range-diff` pairs each old commit with its new version and shows only the real differences, ignoring the noise of the new base. GitHub's "Compare" link after a force-push shows the same idea.

steps.prompt: Start a fix and open a pull request. Put the steps in order.
Which commands only read or download, and which change the remote?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Set `fetch.prune` and `pull.rebase` once, start every branch from a fresh `origin/main`, and never type `--force` without `-with-lease`. When you re-push a PR, paste a `range-diff` or point at the compare link so the reviewer's time goes to the real change.
